transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Start time: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Hawthorne CISO), Evan Malik (HoE), Dr. Lena Brooks (Privacy), Samir Patel (DevOps)

Auto-generated summary: (auto) Discussed Redwood's privacy guarantees including no-training on customer data, KMS/HSM patterns, audit log accessibility, SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/RBAC mapping, and data residency options. Agreed to pilot in isolated VPC with customer-managed KMS.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO attestation, RBAC/SSO (SAML/SCIM), Audit logs & retention, Prompt retention policy / no-training assurance, PHI/PII handling and redaction, On-prem/VPC deployment options, KMS/HSM integration, Next steps and artifacts

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Speaker 1: Okay looks like everyone has joined, starting now. Maya from Redwood, Carlos, Jules. Hi all.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi Priya, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi Maya, yeah this is Priya, Evan, Lena and Samir on my side. Thanks.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. The goal for today is to run through our security posture, make sure our 'no training on customer data' and prompt retention policies align with your procurement requirements, and talk practicals — KMS, audit logs, SSO mapping, residency.
[00:29] Evan Malik: Great. We have a pretty strict requirement from compliance: everything that touches PHI must not be used to update models and we need full auditability.
[00:36] Carlos Ortega: Totally understood. For the 'no training' point — Redwood's hosted tier default is we do not use customer data to train or improve models unless there's an explicit opt-in. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data never leaves their environment and nothing is sent back to model teams.
[00:52] Dr. Lena Brooks: Can you put that in writing? We need contractual language that says customer content will not be used to train models.
[00:59] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include a clause. I'll send standard no-train language and if you need additional wording, legal can iterate.
[01:06] Samir Patel: And the hosted API — is there any caching or retention of prompts after the response that could be used later?
[01:12] Carlos Ortega: Short answer: we have configurable retention. By default we keep logs for X days for debugging, but for enterprise we can set prompt retention to ephemeral or zero-retention and we also support prefix/KV cache that can be customer-controlled in Dedicated and Private modes. Sorry — the transcriber might change some acronyms.
[01:29] Priya Rao: I heard you say 'X days' — can you be specific? Our policy baseline is 7 days max for transient logs and 0 for anything labeled PHI.
[01:36] Carlos Ortega: For hosted we've got a default 30 day window for telemetry; enterprise customers can configure retention down to zero and have a contract addendum for PHI zero-retention. For Dedicated/Private, telemetry can be configured to remain in your VPC.
[01:49] Evan Malik: So for the pilot we need zero retention for prompts marked PHI and separate bucket for audit logs retained for 7 years. Is that feasible?
[01:58] Carlos Ortega: Yes — two separate things: prompt/content retention is separate from audit logs. Audit logs are append-only and can be exported to your S3 or syslog with retention policies you control; we can store for 7 years if you want.
[02:09] Priya Rao: Who signs and stores the audit logs? We need chain-of-custody evidence.
[02:15] Jules Park: For Dedicated/Private we integrate with your S3 and you retain ownership. For hosted we can provide signed, time-stamped log exports and MD5/sha digests on export. There are also options to forward logs to your SIEM in real time.
[02:29] Priya Rao: Okay, that helps. 
[02:33] [02:33] Evan Malik: On KMS — we want customer-managed keys. Do you have HSM integration for on-prem or cloud KMS like AWS KMS w/ external key material?
[02:41] Carlos Ortega: Yes. We support AWS KMS CMKs in both hosted (customer key stored in your account with cross-account grants) and in Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSMs via an adapter for PKCS#11. For Dedicated we can do customer-controlled KMS with bring-your-own-key. We'll share a technical note.
[02:58] Dr. Lena Brooks: How does that interact with model caching or KV cache? If you persist KV cache to speed up generation, is that encrypted with the same key?
[03:08] Carlos Ortega: Good question. KV cache at rest is encrypted with the KMS key binding for that customer. For hosted we rotate keys per-customer; for Dedicated/Private you control rotation. We also support envelope encryption for large objects.
[03:22] Samir Patel: Is the key material ever persisted in Redwood-managed HSMs?
[03:26] Carlos Ortega: Not for customer-managed keys, no. In hosted, if you opt for Redwood-managed keys we maintain them in our HSMs, but customer-managed means the key is in your account/HSM and Redwood only holds a grant.
[03:38] [03:38] Priya Rao: SSO mapping — we need RBAC with SCIM sync to map groups and limit production tokens. Can Redwood enforce per-route RBAC and token scoping?
[03:47] Maya Chen: Yes. We support SAML and OIDC for SSO and SCIM for group sync. RBAC can be enforced at the route and model level; you can scope API keys to specific models or endpoints and restrict token issuance to group membership.
[03:59] Evan Malik: Can we get time-limited tokens that auto-expire in 1 hour for certain dev users?
[04:04] Carlos Ortega: Yes, you can set TTLs on tokens and revoke via the Console or API; we audit token creation.
[04:10] [04:10] Dr. Lena Brooks: Regarding PII/PHI detection — do you offer built-in redaction or do we need to handle at application layer?
[04:17] Carlos Ortega: We have a couple options: inline redaction hooks that can mask entities pre-send, or an SDK filter that runs in your app. For PHI we recommend pre-filtering at runtime and using the no-train + zero-retention for those calls.
[04:30] Priya Rao: Will Redwood sign a BAA for PHI?
[04:34] Maya Chen: We have a template BAA and we've executed BAAs with other healthcare customers; we'll share the template and legal can discuss the rubric.
[04:41] [04:41] Samir Patel: If we go with Private deployment (VPC & on-prem), what network controls exist? Do you support private peering and no internet egress for inference nodes?
[04:51] Carlos Ortega: Yes — Private supports air-gapped or customer VPC-only setups. You can configure no egress, private peering, and restricted management plane. Some telemetry hooks require outbound for updates unless you choose an on-prem bundle.
[05:06] Evan Malik: Latency vs cost question — we might want quantized models for perf. Does quantization change security posture or enable any data leakage?
[05:15] Carlos Ortega: Quantization is purely compute — it doesn't alter data handling. But quantized models sometimes require model variant management; data access controls remain the same.
[05:24] Priya Rao: For legal, we need an auditable statement that Prescott, Redwood engineers, cannot view the raw prompts or responses for our customer in Dedicated/Private.
[05:33] Maya Chen: We'll include language that Redwood engineering access is limited to emergency debugging via an approval workflow with explicit customer approval; and for Dedicated/Private, you can require session-recorded approvals.
[05:44] [05:44] Evan Malik: Can you produce a sample signed export of audit logs showing IP, user id, operation, and sha256 of request payload? We want to test chain-of-custody.
[05:54] Jules Park: Yes we can generate a redacted sample. We'll provide a signed export with digests and a short script to validate signatures.
[06:03] Priya Rao: A few quick clarifications: 1) Are there any implicit A/B tests or model evaluations that could touch our data? 2) If there is a security incident, what is the notification SLAs?
[06:14] Carlos Ortega: 1) No implicit experiments on customer traffic unless you explicitly enroll. For hosted we sometimes run model upgrades but we never use customer prompts for training without consent. 2) Incident response: we have 24/7 SOC, incident initial notification within one hour for Sev 1, follow-up timeline per SLA; we'll include IR runbooks.
[06:32] Dr. Lena Brooks: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs currently?
[06:36] Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II and are ISO 27001 certified; we'll attach the certificates and the latest auditor's report.
[06:44] [06:44] Priya Rao: Does Redwood maintain per-tenant encryption keys for logs, or are logs keyed at account-level?
[06:50] Carlos Ortega: Per-tenant keys for logs, yes. You can also route logs to your own storage so you hold keys.
[06:56] Evan Malik: About model provenance: we need to know which model version handled each request for reproducibility. Can that be logged?
[07:03] Carlos Ortega: Absolutely. Each response includes metadata with model id, exact version/hash, and runtime config. That gets emitted into audit logs and can be included in exports.
[07:13] [07:13] Priya Rao: For data residency — we need all PHI staying in the EU for EU patients. Can you pin inference to specific regions?
[07:20] Maya Chen: Yes. We support region pinning and can route requests to EU-only inference clusters; for Private deployments you can deploy nodes in your chosen region.
[07:30] Samir Patel: One small thing — does the console store prompt examples used in analytics dashboards?
[07:36] Jules Park: The console aggregates telemetry and shows example prompts only if customers opt in to share anonymized examples. For enterprises we default to not show raw examples; you can opt-in at the workspace level.
[07:49] Evan Malik: Ok that makes sense.
[07:52] [07:52] Maya Chen: Alright to recap next steps: I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, BAA template, standard no-train wording. Carlos will share KMS/HSM integration notes and sample audit export. Jules will prepare a redacted example log with signature. Priya, Samir, Evan to confirm residency and acceptance criteria for pilot.
[08:10] Priya Rao: We'll review and get back. We want a pilot in a week if possible.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Great — we'll aim for that. Any final questions?
[08:20] Dr. Lena Brooks: One last thing — can you confirm whether automatic prompt paraphrasing or canonicalization features are off by default? We don't want any normalization that could create additional retention vectors.
[08:30] Carlos Ortega: Those features are opt-in; not applied without explicit config. We'll document defaults in the security packet.
[08:38] Priya Rao: Thanks everyone.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[08:45] End meeting.
